notes: I2 is a judgement call, decided as met. Measured sorbents are the C60-HQ clathrate (HQ3.C60 per the 3:1 stoichiometry), guest-free beta-HQ, MeOH-HQ, CO2-HQ, alpha-HQ and a fullerite (C60) curve, all at 77 K in Figure 4a. By formula mass C60 (about 721 g/mol) is about 69 wt% of HQ3.C60 (3 HQ about 330 g/mol), and carbon is about 89 wt% of the clathrate by elements; this is my arithmetic, not a figure in the paper. The host is an organic H-bonded framework, which is why the call is borderline, but C60 is the majority component and the sorbent is not a MOF, zeolite, hydride or polymer. The paper itself does not say the fullerite curve was measured by the authors, so I2 rests on the C60-HQ clathrate. If a reader holds that a C60-HQ clathrate is not a carbon sorbent, the code would be not_carbon instead of no_surface_area. I1 is met by the gravimetric (magnetic suspension balance, buoyancy-corrected) uptake of the C60-HQ clathrate; the GCMC and DFT parts are computational and are not counted. Other conditions seen: 77 K and 8 MPa for all Figure 4a curves; 93 and 293 K XRD after 30 cycles at 77 K and 8 MPa (SI Figure S9). The article is primary research, is_retracted is false in record.json, and no passage states that all uptake values were published before, so not_primary, retracted and duplicate_data do not apply.
